title: NVIDIA's $500 Billion Financing Is a Hollow Promise: Jensen Huang's Commitments Are Worthless
dek: NVIDIA's so-called $500 billion financing is just a non-binding memorandum of understanding. Jensen Huang previously promised $10 billion to OpenAI but only invested $3 billion, and zero data centers have been built.
why: To debunk NVIDIA's financing theatrics and reveal that its growth relies on circular financing rather than real demand, offering direct insight into the AI bubble.
who: Investors and tech analysts focused on the AI bubble and NVIDIA's valuation, as well as founders who want to understand the inner workings of AI infrastructure financing.
skip: You can skip the introductory guest segment and jump straight to the core analysis.

points.h: The $500 billion financing is just a memorandum of understanding
points.body: Media reports claim NVIDIA is partnering with Apollo, Blackstone, and others to finance $500 billion for AI infrastructure, but in reality, only a memorandum of understanding has been signed, which is not legally binding. The financing will be spread across multiple data center projects, no different from existing practices. NVIDIA has already participated in investments like CoreWeave, so this is not new.

points.h: Huang promised $10 billion to OpenAI but delivered only $3 billion
points.body: In September 2024, Jensen Huang and OpenAI executives announced on CNBC an investment of $100 billion to build 10 gigawatts of compute, but ultimately only $3 billion was invested, and OpenAI has not built any data centers. Huang later claimed he 'never promised,' showing his statements are unreliable.

points.h: The 25% residual value support mechanism is unclear
points.body: Huang tweeted that NVIDIA would provide a 'residual value support mechanism' covering 25% of the opportunity, but did not explain what it means. Speculation is that NVIDIA guarantees the compute revenue of project companies, enabling them to borrow to buy GPUs, similar to CoreWeave's financing model.

points.h: Circular financing: NVIDIA guarantees its own debt
points.body: NVIDIA helps customers raise financing and guarantees their debt, and customers use the loans to buy NVIDIA GPUs, forming a closed loop. This is essentially circular financing because customers lack profitability. Huang claims 'demand is real' yet needs to create demand through debt, which is contradictory.

points.h: The Stargate project is equally hollow
points.body: The $500 billion Stargate project announced in January 2025 by Trump, Altman, and others has actually raised no funds and formed no company; it merely labels OpenAI data centers. NVIDIA's deal is expected to end the same way, with media continuing to endorse it.

points.h: Analysts expect NVIDIA to sell $1.6 trillion in GPUs over three years
points.body: NVIDIA's fiscal 2026 revenue is $216 billion, with analyst expectations of $393.7 billion for 2027, $565.7 billion for 2028, and $694 billion for 2029, totaling over $1.6 trillion. But customers need to borrow to buy, and demand is insufficient to support this.

OpenAI completed a $7 billion internal stock buyback, but the COO left, and the buyback was funded by company cash rather than external investors, which is rare in the industry. Buying back at an $852 billion valuation may reflect internal lack of confidence.
